inputs: docs/specs/fleetd/amendments.md (Revision round 2 and Fix round 2, A19 to A22)
docs/specs/fleetd/amendments.md (Systems review round, fix round 2 and closing fix, A23 to A37)

assumptions.text: The board is to-be: it models fleetd as design.md describes it, not today's horch. Today's differences appear as conflict hotspots H1 to H4 (design.md wins over the other sources, per the run context).
The idea flow has 5 phases (clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating) cut at 4 pivotal events (decision D1, option A, decided by the orchestrator, D15).

Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outside the idea flow (decision D2, option B, decided by the orchestrator, D15). The reconcile loop supervises each phase, not only executing. The operating phase has no pivotal event and no before and after on the idea timeline.

fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3).
The judge, resolver and triage workers are the 'worker' actor running a task of a given kind (understand A5).

The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned, and bundle states) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, removed, orphaned, rescued), and understand N23 and N24 (the task and feature state machines).
'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event.

An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7).

The fleetd command channel, request files while fleetd is down, and the herdr pane mapping are design-level transport; they are not on the board. Request classes, the operator token and the requests table are also transport (understand N25).

Event count 102 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 6 state machines (idea, task, task branch, bundle, feature, worktree) plus jobs; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6.

A state name is never written without the kind of its entity (design A20). The shared names stay: ready (task, task branch, feature) and landed (task branch, worktree). A task is done; its task branch is landed.

open_questions.text: Does an operator requeue also restore the single replan (H12)? Answered part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0, and a requeue by a review keeps its own counter.

external_systems.name: Clock
external_systems.description: The fleetd reconcile pass (every 5 s) and the fixed timers it reads. It fires every time-triggered command. Each operational timer is a deadline on the fleet clock, which does not run while the machine sleeps or while fleetd is down (A25).

external_systems.name: Agent CLI process
external_systems.description: The Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, pi or Prime process of 1 attempt. Its exit is a process fact that the wrapper and the platform layer report.

external_systems.name: git
external_systems.description: Worktrees, branches, refs and merge-tree trial merges. The source of truth for 'in the primary branch by content'.

external_systems.name: GitHub
external_systems.description: Hosts the pull request of a feature (pr setting gh) or the compare URL (pr setting manual).

external_systems.name: OS service manager
external_systems.description: launchd, systemd, or a Windows service and Task Scheduler. Keeps fleetd and herdr running and restarts them.

external_systems.name: Provider pool
external_systems.description: A usage pool of 1 provider (understand actor provider-pool). It reports usage limits, outages and window resets.

external_systems.name: herdr
external_systems.description: The pane runtime in session 'fleet'. Shows panes, agent status and notifications. Holds no state that fleetd depends on.

phases.name: Operating the fleet (outside the idea flow)

events.name: Idea Captured
events.description: horch idea add writes 1 immutable idea file and 1 ledger row in state captured. --to joins an open feature. With no --to, the idea gets a new features row at capture (orchestrator, D15).

events.name: Sub-Orchestrator Started
events.description: fleetd opens pane idea-NNNN with a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the phase. The idea moves to clarifying.

events.name: Interview Question Asked
events.description: The sub-orchestrator asks the operator 1 question in its pane, after it reads the code and docs the idea touches.

events.name: Interview Answer Recorded
events.description: horch idea note appends the question and the answer to interview.md.

events.name: Idea Amended
events.description: horch idea amend adds 1 amendment file. Before approval it joins the interview. After approval it becomes a revise.

events.name: Assumptions Written
events.description: assumptions.md validates with no item marked [open].

events.name: Feature Opened
events.description: fleetd checks the kebab-case name, then creates the feature branch. The features row exists since capture (orchestrator, D15). For a --direct idea with no --to it happens at acceptance.

events.name: Approval Requested
events.description: The idea moves to awaiting_approval. fleetd posts a herdr notification and lists the idea under Needs you. The idea lease is paused.

events.name: Idea Parked
events.description: The idea leaves the queue: 7 days with no answer, an escalation, or horch idea park. Worktrees are rescued first.

events.name: Idea Cancelled
events.description: horch idea cancel. Worktrees are rescued first.

events.name: Assumptions Revised
events.description: horch idea revise sends the idea back to clarifying.

events.name: Assumptions Approved
events.description: horch idea approve, run outside any fleet attempt. fleetd writes approval.json with the hash of the assumptions the operator saw.

events.name: Direct Idea Accepted
events.description: horch idea add --direct: no research and no interview. The idea goes from captured to ticketing. The ticket stands for the approval.

events.name: Spec Written
events.description: spec.md and requirements.yaml validate, and every requirement cites an approved assumption or an operator answer. The idea moves to ticketing.

events.name: Plan Submitted
events.description: The tickets and plan.yaml are on disk for validation.

events.name: Plan Refused
events.description: The plan validator refuses the plan, for example a judgment task with no paired judge, or a project with no declared fast and full gate. A refused --direct plan goes to needs-you/.

events.name: Plan Committed
events.description: The plan passes validation and its tasks commit in 1 transaction. The idea moves to in_progress. No task exists outside a committed plan.

events.name: Plan Verdict Written
events.description: The plan validator writes plan.verdict.json for the sub-orchestrator: committed or refused. A refusal carries its reasons (connect A10).

events.name: Task Promoted
events.description: Every dependency of the task is done, or its quota pool reset, or the operator requeued it.

events.name: Task Leased
events.description: fleetd binds the task to a new attempt. In the same transaction it writes the worktree row (reserved) and the task branch row (building).

events.name: Worktree Created
events.description: The worktree_add job passed, and the next pass sees the directory. The attempt launches only after it. A retried attempt reuses the existing worktree (A32).

events.name: Attempt Launched
events.description: fleetd writes task.yaml and inbox/START.md for the attempt. The start of the process follows as Agent Process Started.

events.name: Agent Process Started
events.description: The fleet-run wrapper and the CLI run in their own process group, started through the platform layer and the herdr adapter with the launch environment of the profile.

events.name: Heartbeat Written
events.description: The fleet-run wrapper (worker-profiles), not the model, rewrites heartbeat.json every 10 s. Renew Lease reads it as an outside signal (connect A10).

events.name: Lease Renewed
events.description: The process is alive, the heartbeat is under 30 s old, and there was activity within stall_after.

events.name: Lease Expired
events.description: No earned renewal before the deadline on the fleet clock. For a resolver attempt or a fix attempt of a done task, the expiry ends that attempt and adds 1 to repair_attempts of its branch, and the task does not move (A25, A37).

events.name: Agent Status Changed
events.description: herdr reports the agent status of a pane through its socket events: working, blocked on a dialog, or idle. The stall ladder reads it (connect A10).

events.name: Attempt Stalled
events.description: The stall ladder reached its last rung: idle with no result after 2 doorbells, hung, no first signal in 90 s, or blocked on a permission dialog.

events.name: Usage Limit Reported
events.description: The worker shows a usage limit or a provider outage. This is not a stall and burns no attempt. The attempt ends with the outcome quota, which burns no attempt (A26).

events.name: Fallback Persona Assigned
events.description: The fallback persona is on another provider: the task restarts at once on a new worker of the fallback, on the same worktree.

events.name: Quota Wait Started
events.description: No fallback on another provider: the task waits in waiting_quota with its lease paused. fleetd does not go to a third persona.

events.name: Quota Window Reset
events.description: The usage window of the pool resets.

events.name: Worker Question Asked
events.description: The worker writes 1 question file, commits its work in progress and exits. The attempt ends with the outcome asked, which burns no attempt, and the task moves to blocked_on_user with no process. The question is a ledger row with an owner and a time limit (A26).

events.name: Question Answered
events.description: The approved assumptions or the spec cover the question; fleetd checks that the cited line exists. Or the sub-orchestrator replans the task.

events.name: Own Assumption Recorded
events.description: Nothing approved covers the question and it changes no assumption: the sub-orchestrator decides and records a reversible assumption marked as its own decision (D13).

events.name: Revise Requested
events.description: The answer changes an approved assumption. It goes to the operator as a revise. Only the affected tasks pause.

events.name: Question Escalated
events.description: The question passed its time limit. It goes to needs-you/ with a herdr notification.

events.name: Result Written
events.description: outbox/result.json lands. A stop hook, or the wrapper repair pass, refuses to end the attempt without it.

events.name: Attempt Exited
events.description: The CLI process group exited. The wrapper writes exit.json. Exec mode turns 'stopped' into 'process exited'.

events.name: Check Passed
events.description: The verifier ran the acceptance commands (or the structural check for a judgment or judge kind) in the worktree, in the sandbox of the worker, within the check timeout.

events.name: Check Failed
events.description: An acceptance command failed. The claim of the worker does not count.

events.name: Review Passed
events.description: Code kind only: today's review scripts pass unchanged (code-sweep rounds, findings F<n>, answers file, waivers).

events.name: Review Failed
events.description: The review scripts requeue the task (at most 2 requeues).

events.name: Judge Verdict Written
events.description: The paired judge task, in another session and on another provider when the roster has one, ranks each miss CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW.

events.name: Critical Fix Opened
events.description: A CRITICAL miss blocks. The attempt of the judge task ends with the outcome critical_open, which burns no attempt. A fix round is a new attempt of the judged task and then of the judge task, counted in fix_rounds of the judged task (A26).

events.name: High Finding Settled
events.description: A HIGH miss does not block alone. The sub-orchestrator fixes it or dismisses it with a written reason.

events.name: Attempt Failed
events.description: 1 state for every non-verified outcome: stalled, no_result, lease expired, check failed. fleetd stops the process group and requeues in 1 transaction before any signal.

events.name: Retry Scheduled
events.description: Attempts remain: a new attempt starts after backoff (30 s, 2 min, 8 min) in the same worktree with a handoff file.

events.name: Replan Requested
events.description: No attempts remain: the task goes to the sub-orchestrator of its idea to replan once.

events.name: Task Replanned
events.description: The sub-orchestrator changes the failed task. The changed plan validates again.

events.name: Task Escalated
events.description: The replan failed too, or 2 fix rounds left a CRITICAL item, or a rescue failed verification. The task goes to needs-you/.

events.name: Task Requeued
events.description: An operator requeue resets the attempt count (04 L8) and resumes on the same worktree (04 L5).

events.name: Worktree Orphaned
events.description: The reconciler finds a tree with no live owner, or a directory with no row. A tree that vanished without fleetd is escalated.

events.name: Worktree Rescued
events.description: fleetd commits the full tree to refs/horch/rescue/<task>/<n> with a private index and verifies it byte for byte before any removal.

events.name: Rescue Failed
events.description: The rescue commit does not match the tree. The tree stays in place.

events.name: Task Done
events.description: Only the verifier moves a task to done: the check passed, then the review (code kind), or the judge with no CRITICAL item (judgment kind).

events.name: Task Verdict Written
events.description: The verifier writes verdict.json, its decision for the attempt, for the sub-orchestrator (connect A10).

events.name: Task Branch Verified
events.description: The task branch leaves verifying and waits for the next bundle.

events.name: Bundle Built
events.description: 1 candidate from the feature branch tip plus each ready task branch in queue order. Each task keeps its commits.

events.name: Task Branch Conflicted
events.description: The rebase of the task branch conflicts. The same worker resolves it (today's behavior).

events.name: Fast Gate Passed
events.description: The unit tests of the project pass once on the candidate.

events.name: Fast Gate Failed
events.description: The fast gate fails on the candidate.

events.name: Task Branch Landed
events.description: Under the land lock, after the check that the task is still held (04 F9), the feature branch fast-forwards to the candidate.

events.name: Task Branch Gate Failed
events.description: fleetd bisects the bundle. The failing branch goes to gate_failed; the others go on.

events.name: Triage Task Opened
events.description: A gate failure becomes a triage task of the feature, owned by its sub-orchestrator.

events.name: Task Branch Abandoned
events.description: Only the operator abandons a task branch. A rescue ref is kept.

events.name: Worktree Removed
events.description: Nothing in the tree is unique any more. fleetd removes it, and deletes the branch only when it is merged and no git stash entry names it (04 W6).

events.name: Idea Task Branches Landed
events.description: The task branch of every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch. The idea moves to integrating.

events.name: Primary Branch Moved
events.description: The fetch job saw that the remote tip of the base branch of the project moved. With remote = none, fleetd reads the local primary branch (A23, A28).

events.name: Trial Merge Passed
events.description: git merge-tree --write-tree with no checkout. The result is a ledger fact.

events.name: Trial Merge Conflicted
events.description: 2 in-flight features, or a feature and the primary branch, conflict.

events.name: Feature Stacked
events.description: The younger feature is put on top of the older one.

events.name: Resolver Task Opened
events.description: 1 code-kind task for a fresh agent with the conflict in zdiff3 form and the requirements and unit tests of both features. It lands on the younger feature branch.

events.name: Feature Branch Rebased
events.description: Bottom of a stack first. A rescue ref of the old tip is written before the rebase. The fast gate runs again.

events.name: Feature Rebase Conflicted
events.description: The rebase conflicts. The conflict becomes a resolver task.

events.name: Full Gate Passed
events.description: The fast gate plus the end-to-end tests pass on the feature tip over the current primary branch. The pass is stale once either tip moves.

events.name: Full Gate Failed
events.description: Failures become triage tasks of the feature.

events.name: Feature Marked Ready
events.description: The feature has a fresh full gate pass.

events.name: Pull Request Opened
events.description: fleetd pushes the feature branch. pr gh opens the pull request, pr manual shows the compare URL. A stacked feature's pull request has the lower feature branch as its base.

events.name: Pull Request Merged
events.description: By default the operator merges. A project setting can say otherwise.

events.name: Feature Merged
events.description: fleetd reads from git, by content, that the feature changes are in the primary branch. This holds for a squash merge.

events.name: Idea Merged
events.description: Terminal. Every worktree of the idea is removed. The closing note lists any rescue ref that never landed.

events.name: Fleetd Hang Detected
events.description: horch fleetd check (launchd timer, Windows scheduled task, every horch command) or the systemd watchdog sees no full pass for 30 s of awake time.

events.name: New Horch Version Installed
events.description: horch self-update replaces the binary.

events.name: Fleetd Restarted
events.description: fleetd starts again and recovers from the ledger and the files. It exits only between passes (04 S7).

events.name: Adapter Conformance Failed
events.description: Docs sync (daily, plus on a CLI version change) ran the conformance test of an adapter and it failed.

events.name: Profile Marked Unhealthy
events.description: The profile gets no new dispatch until a conformance test passes. A permission dialog in an attempt does the same.

events.name: Task Cancelled
events.description: A replan that replaces the task, horch task cancel, or the cancel or abandon of its idea or feature. fleetd first stops the process group of a live attempt, then moves the task to cancelled. The cancel of a judged task also cancels its judge task (A34).

events.name: Bundle Dropped
events.description: A member conflicted in the build, the feature tip moved while the bundle was building or gating, or the compare-and-set of the ref move failed. The members go back to ready (A27, A34).

events.name: Task Branch Repair Escalated
events.description: A resolver attempt or a fix attempt of a done task failed at max_attempts. repair_attempts of the branch reached the limit, and 1 item goes on the needs-you list. The task stays done (A34).

events.name: Remote Tips Recorded
events.description: The periodic fetch job (fetch_period_s, 60 s) recorded the remote tip of each branch in remote_tips. A failed fetch sets stale_since (A23).

events.name: Feature Branch Pushed
events.description: The push job of the feature branch passed. A push that rewrites uses --force-with-lease on seen_remote_tip (A27, A28).

events.name: Push Failed
events.description: The push job failed. push_state is failed, push_failures goes up by 1, and the next run waits for push_not_before. At 3 failures in a row, 1 item goes on the needs-you list (A28, A33).

events.name: Feature Reopened
events.description: A ready feature goes back to open: its tip or the fetched primary tip moved, or a new idea was accepted with --to. fleetd marks its pull request as a draft (A28).

events.name: Pull Request Closed
events.description: The operator closed the pull request without a merge. pr_state is closed, and 1 item goes on the needs-you list (A28).

events.name: In-Flight Ideas Moved
events.description: The operator merged the pull request while an idea of the feature was in flight. fleetd records the feature as merged and moves each such idea to a new feature (A28).

events.name: Feature Abandoned
events.description: Only the operator sets it, with horch feature abandon. fleetd first writes a rescue ref for each branch of the feature that is not landed, then moves each such branch to abandoned and cancels each idea of the feature that is not terminal (A28).

events.name: Adapter Conformance Passed
events.description: Each conformance check of an adapter passed, the check Operator boundary included (A35).

events.name: Profile Marked Healthy
events.description: worker-profiles marks the profile healthy again when its conformance checks pass. fleetd dispatches to it again.

events.name: Job Abandoned
events.description: A job was stopped at its time limit, or its process was lost. It has no verdict. Its next run waits for the job backoff. At abandoned_run_limit (3) no new run starts, and 1 item goes on the needs-you list (A23, A33).

events.name: Job Requeued
events.description: horch job requeue sets abandoned_runs of the job key to 0, and the next run starts (A33).

events.name: Rescue Ref Dropped
events.description: horch rescue drop deletes a rescue ref of class unique. Only the operator deletes a unique rescue ref (A27, I10).

commands.name: Add Idea
commands.description: horch idea add "..." or -f notes.md, optional --to <feature>.

commands.name: Start Sub-Orchestrator
commands.description: fleetd starts 1 fresh process per phase in the pane of the feature, and restarts a dead or missing one on the next pass.

commands.name: Ask Operator
commands.description: 1 question at a time: what done looks like, scope edges, constraints, affected areas, priority.

commands.name: Answer Interview Question
commands.description: The operator answers in the pane. horch idea note records it.

commands.name: Amend Idea
commands.description: horch idea amend <id> "...".

commands.name: Write Assumptions
commands.description: Writes assumptions.md: [confirmed] and [assumed] items, none [open].

commands.name: Open Feature
commands.description: Creates the feature branch of the features row that capture wrote.

commands.name: Request Approval
commands.description: Moves the idea to awaiting_approval and notifies the operator. Reminds once an hour in working hours.

commands.name: Park Idea
commands.description: Issued by policy after 7 days of waiting or an escalation. The operator also runs horch idea park.

commands.name: Cancel Idea
commands.description: horch idea cancel.

commands.name: Revise Assumptions
commands.description: horch idea revise <id> "...".

commands.name: Approve Assumptions
commands.description: horch idea approve <id>. Refused inside any fleet attempt; profiles deny it.

commands.name: Add Direct Idea
commands.description: horch idea add --direct <ticket file>, optional --to. Refused inside a fleet attempt.

commands.name: Write Spec
commands.description: Writes spec.md and requirements.yaml after approval.

commands.name: Submit Plan
commands.description: Writes tickets and plan.yaml.

commands.name: Validate Plan
commands.description: The plan validator: paired judges, declared gates, model guide, overlapping paths. Commits tasks in 1 transaction.

commands.name: Promote Task
commands.description: pending to ready when every dependency is done, or waiting_quota to ready when the pool resets.

commands.name: Dispatch Task
commands.description: No cap. Only the health guards (free disk, load) and the pacing of the pool hold dispatch.

commands.name: Create Worktree
commands.description: git worktree add on the task branch. Only fleetd creates worktrees. It runs as a worktree_add job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Launch Attempt
commands.description: Starts the wrapper and the CLI in its own process group. A resume after an answer also launches.

commands.name: Assign Task
commands.description: fleetd writes task.yaml for the attempt from the committed plan, before the launch. It is atomic and never rewritten; a change is a new attempt. The worker reads it (connect A10).

commands.name: Start Work
commands.description: fleetd writes inbox/START.md, the first file the worker reads, before the launch. Its path is the launch argument (connect A10).

commands.name: Start Agent Process
commands.description: Starts the fleet-run wrapper of an attempt, or the herdr pane of a sub-orchestrator, from the launch environment. The sub-orchestrator start sends it too.

commands.name: Renew Lease
commands.description: Every reconcile pass (5 s). Lease time counts only while the machine is awake.

commands.name: Apply Stall Ladder
commands.description: Every pass: doorbell, doorbell after 2 min, then end. stall_after default 5 min; start timeout 90 s.

commands.name: Move To Fallback
commands.description: Fallback persona on another provider, else waiting_quota with the lease paused.

commands.name: Ask Question
commands.description: Writes 1 question file, commits work in progress, exits.

commands.name: Answer Question
commands.description: fleetd starts the owner on each pass until an answer is recorded. 4 cases (design, Ideas, How a worker's question is resolved).

commands.name: Escalate Question
commands.description: Fires when a running sub-orchestrator has not answered the question in 15 min (a starting value, orchestrator D15). The wait for the operator has no limit.

commands.name: Write Result
commands.description: horch result writes outbox/result.json.

commands.name: Run Check
commands.description: The verifier, with today's check timeout (20 min, max 24 h). It runs as a task_check job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Run Review
commands.description: Today's review scripts, unchanged. Rounds: light 1, full 3.

commands.name: Write Judge Verdict
commands.description: The worker of a judge task writes its verdict file.

commands.name: Open Critical Fix
commands.description: At most 2 fix rounds.

commands.name: Settle High Finding
commands.description: Fix or dismiss with a written reason.

commands.name: End Attempt
commands.description: Stops the process group through the platform layer (Linux: SIGINT, 20 s, SIGKILL).

commands.name: Schedule Retry
commands.description: Reads max_attempts and backoff from the profile.

commands.name: Replan Task
commands.description: Once per task.

commands.name: Escalate Task
commands.description: Writes to needs-you/ and posts a herdr notification.

commands.name: Requeue Task
commands.description: Resets attempt_floor.

commands.name: Reconcile Worktrees
commands.description: Every pass reads rows and /fleet/work; every 60 s also git worktree list --porcelain.

commands.name: Rescue Worktree
commands.description: Private index, commit-tree, update-ref, then verify. It runs as a rescue job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Mark Task Done
commands.description: The verifier writes verdict.json.

commands.name: Check Fleetd
commands.description: Every 30 s on macOS and Windows; WatchdogSec=30 on Linux; before each horch command.

commands.name: Self Update
commands.description: horch self-update. The operator runs it too.

commands.name: Restart Fleetd
commands.description: Restart always, through the platform layer.

commands.name: Run Conformance Tests
commands.description: Daily plus on any CLI version change. It runs as a conformance job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Mark Profile Unhealthy
commands.description: Blocks new dispatch on the profile.

commands.name: Mark Branch Ready
commands.description: verifying to ready.

commands.name: Build Bundle
commands.description: 1 bundle per feature from the ready task branches in queue order. It runs as a bundle_build job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Run Fast Gate
commands.description: The declared fast gate of the project. It runs as a fast_gate job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Fast-Forward Feature Branch
commands.description: Land lock 1 h, 5 tries. A red land resets to the tip before the rebase (04 F7).

commands.name: Bisect Bundle
commands.description: Finds the failing task branch.

commands.name: Open Triage Task
commands.description: A task of the feature for a gate failure.

commands.name: Abandon Task Branch
commands.description: Operator only.

commands.name: Remove Worktree
commands.description: Only after landed or a verified rescue. It runs as a worktree_remove job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Roll Up Idea
commands.description: in_progress to integrating.

commands.name: Run Trial Merges
commands.description: Each in-flight feature against the primary branch and against each other in-flight feature. It runs as a trial_merge job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Stack Feature
commands.description: Sets stacked_on to the older feature.

commands.name: Open Resolver Task
commands.description: At most 100 changed lines or 2 files, else split by file. rerere is on.

commands.name: Rebase Feature Branch
commands.description: Writes a rescue ref of the old tip first. It runs as a rebase job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Run Full Gate
commands.description: Once for a feature when the task branches of its tasks are landed, again when a pass goes stale. It runs as a full_gate job outside the reconcile pass (A23, A32).

commands.name: Mark Feature Ready
commands.description: features.state open to ready.

commands.name: Open Pull Request
commands.description: pr setting gh or manual.

commands.name: Merge Pull Request
commands.description: On GitHub, or a plain git merge. The default merger is the operator.

commands.name: Check Merged
commands.description: Every pass reads git, not the GitHub API.

commands.name: Close Idea
commands.description: Needs every worktree of the idea removed.

commands.name: Cancel Task
commands.description: horch task cancel. A policy also issues it for a replan that replaces the task and for the cancel or abandon of its idea or feature (A34).

commands.name: Escalate Task Branch
commands.description: Puts a task branch on the needs-you list when repair_attempts reaches max_attempts.

commands.name: Fetch Remote
commands.description: Queues 1 fetch job for each repository at each fetch period. It is an effect job outside the reconcile pass (A23).

commands.name: Push Feature Branch
commands.description: Queues a push job of the feature branch. Each retry is a new run of the job (A33).

commands.name: Reopen Feature
commands.description: Moves a ready feature back to open and marks its pull request as a draft.

commands.name: Abandon Feature
commands.description: horch feature abandon.

commands.name: Move Ideas To New Feature
commands.description: Moves each idea in flight of a merged feature to a new feature.

commands.name: Mark Profile Healthy

policies.name: Whenever an idea is captured, start a sub-orchestrator for its feature
Whenever assumptions are written for an idea with no feature branch, open the feature
Whenever the feature of an idea with valid assumptions is open, request approval
Whenever assumptions are revised, start a fresh sub-orchestrator in clarifying
Whenever approval is requested and 7 days pass with no answer, park the idea
Whenever assumptions are approved, start a fresh sub-orchestrator in specifying
Whenever a direct idea with no --to is accepted, open a feature named from the ticket title
Whenever a plan is submitted, validate it
Whenever a direct plan is refused, escalate it to needs-you
Whenever a plan is committed, promote the tasks with no dependencies
Whenever a task is ready, dispatch it unless a health guard or pacing holds it
Whenever a task is leased, create its worktree unless one exists
Whenever a worktree is created for a leased task, launch the attempt
Whenever an attempt is launched, write task.yaml and START.md, then start its agent process
Whenever an attempt stalls, end the attempt
Whenever a lease expires, end the attempt
Whenever a usage limit is reported, move the task to its fallback or to waiting_quota
Whenever a task moves to its fallback, launch a new attempt on the same worktree
Whenever a quota window resets, promote the tasks waiting on that pool
Whenever a worker asks a question, start its owner sub-orchestrator until an answer is recorded
Whenever a question is answered, resume the worker session with the answer
Whenever the sub-orchestrator records its own assumption, resume the worker session
Whenever a revise is requested, the operator approves or revises the changed assumption
Whenever an attempt exits with a result, run its check
Whenever an attempt exits with commits and no result, resume once to write the result
Whenever the check of a code-kind task passes, run the review scripts
Whenever the structural check of a judge task passes, mark it done
Whenever a check fails, end the attempt as failed
Whenever the review passes, mark the task done
Whenever the review fails, end the attempt as failed
Whenever a judge verdict is written, mark the judged task done with no CRITICAL, else open a fix
Whenever a judge verdict has a HIGH finding, the sub-orchestrator fixes or dismisses it
Whenever a second critical fix still leaves a CRITICAL item, escalate the task
Whenever an attempt fails, retry after backoff or request a replan
Whenever a retry is scheduled, launch the next attempt in the same worktree after backoff
Whenever a replan is requested, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once
Whenever a task is replanned, promote it
Whenever the operator requeues a task, promote it
Whenever a worktree is orphaned, rescue it before any cleanup
Whenever a rescue fails verification, escalate
Whenever a task is done, mark its task branch ready
Whenever the fleetd heartbeat goes stale, restart fleetd
Whenever the horch binary is updated, restart fleetd on the new binary
Whenever adapter conformance fails, mark the profile unhealthy
Whenever a task branch is ready, add it to the next bundle of its feature
Whenever a bundle is built, run the fast gate on it
Whenever a task branch conflicts, the same worker resolves the rebase
Whenever the fast gate passes, fast-forward the feature branch
Whenever the fast gate fails, bisect the bundle
Whenever a task branch fails the gate, start a fix attempt of its task in its worktree
Whenever a task branch lands, remove its worktree, roll up the idea and run trial merges
Whenever the task branch of every task of an idea is landed, run the full gate of its feature
Whenever the primary branch moves, rebase each feature branch and run trial merges
Whenever a trial merge of 2 features conflicts, stack the younger feature on the older one
Whenever a feature is stacked, open 1 resolver task
Whenever a feature rebase conflicts, open a resolver task
Whenever a feature branch is rebased, run the fast gate again
Whenever the full gate passes, mark the feature ready
Whenever the full gate fails, open triage tasks of the feature
Whenever a feature is ready, push it and open its pull request
Whenever a pull request is opened, the operator reviews and merges it
Whenever a feature is merged, close each of its ideas once their worktrees are removed
Whenever a task is escalated, the operator requeues or abandons it
Whenever an idea is cancelled, cancel each of its tasks that is not terminal
Whenever a task is cancelled, write a rescue ref of its task branch and abandon the branch
Whenever a critical fix is opened, start a fix attempt of the judged task
Whenever the structural check of a judged task passes, keep it in verifying and promote its judge task
Whenever a bundle is dropped, build the next bundle from the ready members
Whenever a resolver or fix attempt fails at max_attempts, put its task branch on the needs-you list
Whenever a task branch repair is escalated, the operator requeues the task or abandons the branch
Whenever a push fails, push again after the backoff
Whenever a pull request is closed without a merge, the operator abandons the feature
Whenever a feature is abandoned, cancel its ideas and abandon its branches that are not landed
Whenever a feature is merged with ideas in flight, move them to a new feature
Whenever a lower feature of a stack is merged, rebase the upper feature on the primary tip
Whenever adapter conformance passes, mark its profiles healthy
Whenever adapter conformance fails, queue an idea to update the adapter
Whenever a job key reaches the abandoned run limit, the operator requeues the job

hotspots.text: Today a worker 'claims' a task and the 'task' row carries the run; fleetd splits this into task (planned unit from plan.yaml), attempt (1 run of 1 worker: A1, A2) and lease (the time-limited hold that renews only on earned activity). Readers of today's ledger and code will read 'task' where fleetd means 'attempt' (understand N1).

'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)?

'Orchestrator' today is 1 long-lived LLM conversation that receives ideas, creates tasks and reads mail. In fleetd it does not exist: a deterministic idea dispatcher and 1 sub-orchestrator per feature replace it. Today's mail contract still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers (understand N3).

'Done' today is a model action (horch ledger done / horch done). In fleetd only the verifier moves a task to done, and 'landed' (on the feature branch) and 'merged' (in the primary branch by content) are later, separate facts. A reader can take 'done' to mean the work reached the primary branch (understand N4).

'Judgment kind' (research, design, docs, report, creative) and the kind 'judge' sound alike. A judgment task needs a paired judge task; a judge task needs no judge. A resolver task has a code kind. Mixing them breaks plan validation (understand N12).

'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle; a feature is ready when its full gate passed. 'Landed' is both a task branch state and a worktree state. Which one does a status line mean? Answered (design A20): the state names stay, and each status line, event, log line and message that gives a state also gives the kind of its entity. A task is done; its task branch is landed.

The idea row records its feature (ideas.feature_id), but the feature row and branch are written when the sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions. Which feature does an idea with no --to point at between capture and assumptions, and what does horch ideas show for it? Answered (orchestrator, D15): the idea gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions.

The Preservation analysis rows (04 W6, F9, F7, F5, L5, L9, W8, W9, F11, S7, L6, L8, S8, S10, M5, 05 E-10, 06 S1 to S15) are hard inputs. Each must have exactly 1 owner in the model; a row that falls between 2 owners is a behavior fleetd silently drops (understand N15).
What number counts as 'full use' of the subscription usage that pacing aims for? Pacing holds dispatch per pool window, but the design gives no target (understand Q1).

A worker question has 'a time limit' before it escalates, but the design gives no value for it, and it does not say if the limit pauses while the operator is outside working hours. Answered (orchestrator, D15): 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, as a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit.

Plan validation refuses a project that has not declared a fast gate and a full gate, and this repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10, understand Q8). Until one is declared, no plan of this repository can commit.

A task gets max_attempts attempts, then 1 replan, then goes to the operator. A requeue resets attempt_floor (04 L8). Does a requeued task also get a new replan, and how does the 2-requeue limit of the review scripts count against attempts? Answered in part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0; a review requeue keeps its own counter. The replan stays open (Q3).

Lease and stall time count only while the machine is awake. If the platform layer reports sleep and wake wrongly on 1 OS, leases expire during a sleep and every worker burns an attempt at wake. Answered (design A25): each timer is a deadline on 1 fleet clock in the ledger, which does not run while the machine sleeps or while fleetd is down. The hang check of fleetd and max_minutes of the wrapper use awake time from the platform layer.

Docs sync and adapter conformance are collapsed to 2 events here. The flow that turns a drift into a task (who owns it, how a profile becomes healthy again) is not stormed. Answered (design, Docs sync and adapter conformance): docs sync is a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules as a docs_sync job, then a conformance job. worker-profiles marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again, and a drift becomes an idea.

A project setting says who merges a feature; the default is the operator. When the setting lets fleetd merge, which gate and which actor stands for the merge decision? Answered (design A28, the feature state table): the owner of a ready feature is the operator, or fleetd when the project sets the merge to automatic. The gate is the full gate on the feature tip over the fetched primary tip.

scenarios.name: Happy path: 1 rough idea becomes 1 merged feature
A usage limit moves the task to its fallback persona with no burned attempt
A worker stalls, its tree is kept, and the retry continues the same work
2 in-flight features conflict and are stacked with 1 resolver task
An idea is cancelled: its tasks are cancelled, and each task branch is rescued and abandoned

glossary.definition: A rough request from the operator that 1 fixed state machine moves from captured to merged; only code advances it.
avoid: ticket (a ticket enters as a --direct idea)

glossary.definition: 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request to the primary branch, holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. The task kind 'feature' is a different thing (H2).
The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase.
1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; the sub-orchestrator can also record its own reversible one.
The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan.
A planned unit of work from plan.yaml with a kind, a check and an owner path set; it survives many attempts (H1).
1 run of 1 worker on 1 task (A1, A2, ...), launched through the wrapper and ended by fleetd.
The time-limited hold of an attempt on its task that renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota.
The git working tree that fleetd leases to 1 task before it exists and never removes before its work is landed or rescued.
A verified commit under refs/horch/rescue/ that saves the full state of a tree or an old branch tip before cleanup or rebase.
The branch of 1 task that lands on its feature branch through the landing state machine.
The branch of 1 feature that collects its landed task branches and reaches the primary branch through 1 pull request.
The base branch of a project; main in this repository, not in every project.
1 candidate made from the feature branch tip plus every ready task branch of that feature, tested once by the fast gate.
The declared unit-test command of a project that every bundle and every rebased feature branch must pass.
The fast gate plus the end-to-end tests, run on a feature tip over the current primary branch; a pass goes stale when either tip moves.
A merge-tree result between 2 in-flight features, or a feature and the primary branch, recorded in the ledger with no checkout.
A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files.
A task of kind judge that ranks the misses of 1 judgment-kind task CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW; it needs no judge itself (H5).
The persona that a worker persona names for use when its provider pool shows a usage limit or an outage.

A piece of work that can take more than 1 s, run in its own process outside the reconcile pass and recorded as a jobs row. A pure job has a verdict that is used again; an effect job runs again each time.
The count of seconds in the fleetd row of the ledger that each pass advances by at most 2 pass periods. Every operational deadline uses it, so a sleep fires no deadline.

decisions.question: Where are the pivotal events that cut the fleetd timeline into phases?

options.summary: 4 pivotal events (assumptions approved, plan committed, task done, idea tasks landed) and 5 phases: clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating.
pros: Each pivotal event is a state change of the design: approval gate, plan commit, verifier verdict, landed roll-up
Matches the actor changes in N7
cons: Planning is a short phase with 5 events
risks: Decompose may split planning from clarifying although 1 sub-orchestrator does both

options.summary: 2 pivotal events (assumptions approved, task done) and 3 phases: shaping, building, integrating.
pros: Fewer, broader phases; the conservative reading
cons: Hides the landing state machine inside building or integrating
Hides the plan commit, the moment a task can first exist
risks: Landing and feature integration look like 1 context

options.summary: 5 pivotal events (add task done split from verification, so a separate verifying phase) and 6 phases.
pros: Makes the verifier a visible phase, as the design stresses 'done is a fact on disk'
cons: Verification interleaves with attempts (check failed loops back to an attempt), so the phase edge is not a before and after
risks: Decompose cuts a verifier context that cannot decide alone

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommendation: A. The design names an approval gate, a plan commit, a verifier verdict and a landed roll-up as distinct facts. Strongest argument against A: clarifying and planning are 1 sub-orchestrator on 1 idea folder, so the cut between them may not be a context boundary.
would_flip_if: The operator treats planning as part of clarifying
The operator wants the verifier as its own phase

decisions.question: Where do daemon supervision and adapter conformance sit on the timeline?

options.summary: At the end of the executing phase, because they act on running attempts and profiles.
cons: They are not part of 1 idea's flow
risks: Decompose reads them as part of task execution

options.summary: In their own 'operating' phase outside the idea flow.
pros: Shows that they run on a schedule for the whole fleet
cons: A phase with no before and after on the idea timeline
risks: A 6th phase that is not on the timeline confuses connect

options.summary: Off the board, as a missing hotspot only.
cons: Drops 04 S10 (restart on new binary) and the conformance gate from the model
risks: A preservation row has no owner

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommendation: A, recorded as assumption A3. Strongest argument against A: these events have no idea or task in their data, so they belong to a fleet-wide context, which B shows more honestly. The orchestrator chose B, not the recommendation A. Reason: the reconcile loop supervises each phase (sub-orchestrators in clarifying, landing rows, questions), not only executing.
would_flip_if: Decompose finds a separate daemon or platform context

notes_for_downstream.text: H1 sharpens understand N1: the board gives task and attempt their own aggregate candidates, and the lease events (lease-renewed, lease-expired) belong to the attempt, not the task.
H2 sharpens understand N2: the feature aggregate owns feature-opened to feature-merged; the task kind 'feature' (a code kind) is a different meaning of the same word.

H3 sharpens understand N3: every dispatcher command on the board has actor null (policy) or clock; today's mail contract (05 C-1) still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers, so the word survives in a preserved contract.

H4 sharpens understand N4: done (verifier), landed (on the feature branch) and merged (in the primary branch by content) are 3 facts at 3 pivotal moments: task-done, idea-tasks-landed, feature-merged.
H5 sharpens understand N12: on the board the judge verdict, critical fix and high finding events belong to the verification of the judged task, not to the judge task.

H6, answered by design A20: 'ready' is a task state, a task branch state and a feature state; 'landed' is a task branch state and a worktree state. The names stay. Each context that owns one state machine owns its own meaning, and each status line, event, log line and message names the entity kind with the state.

The actor changes on the board: operator and sub-orchestrator own clarifying and planning; workers and the clock-driven reconcile pass own executing; fleetd code alone owns landing and integrating, with the operator back only at the pull request merge. The 4 pivotal events sit on those changes.

H8 sharpens understand N15: the Worktree and Task branch aggregates own most no-loss preservation rows (04 W6, W8, W9, F5, F7, F9, F11, L5, L9); Task and Attempt own S7, S8, L6, L8; the daemon owns S10. Each row needs exactly 1 owning context.

D2 option B (orchestrator, D15): the board has a 6th phase, operating, outside the idea flow. It holds fleetd-hang-detected, horch-version-installed, fleetd-restarted, adapter-conformance-failed and profile-marked-unhealthy. The reconcile loop supervises every phase, so these events carry no idea or task.

Answers connect Q2: discover adopts the ids of connect. start-agent-process is a command (event agent-process-started, policy start-process-on-launch). launch-environment and trial-merge-result are read models, which connect models as queries.

Q1 answered (orchestrator, D15): an idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions. idea-captured always carries featureId; feature-opened creates only the branch.

Q2 and Q3 answers (orchestrator, D15): a worker question escalates to the operator after 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator (a starting value); the wait for the operator has no limit. An operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0; a review requeue keeps its own counter. Whether an operator requeue restores the replan stays open (Q3).

Answers connect Q6: discover adopts the 6 ids of connect with the types of connect. assign-task and start-work are commands (both lead to attempt-launched). heartbeat-written, task-verdict-written, plan-verdict-written and agent-status-changed are events.

The bundle is its own state machine (building, gating, passed, landed, failed, dropped) with its rows in bundles and bundle_members (A27, A34). On the board its events sit on the task-branch aggregate. fleetd owns conflicted and gate_failed: a resolver attempt or fix attempt of a done task is an attempt of the task branch, and its failure counts in repair_attempts of the branch, not in the attempts of the task.

Long work is a job (A23, A32, A33). These commands queue a job and do not wait: run-check (task_check), build-bundle (bundle_build), run-fast-gate (fast_gate), run-full-gate (full_gate), run-trial-merges (trial_merge), rebase-feature-branch (rebase), rescue-worktree (rescue), create-worktree (worktree_add), remove-worktree (worktree_remove), fetch-remote (fetch), push-feature-branch (push), run-conformance-tests (conformance). The job aggregate owns job-abandoned and job-requeued.

Task cancel (A34): each task state that is not terminal exits to cancelled through cancel-task. The policies cancel-tasks-on-idea-cancelled, cancel-on-feature-abandoned and abandon-branch-on-task-cancelled give the order: stop the process group, cancel the task, write a rescue ref, abandon the branch. The outcomes asked, quota and critical_open burn no attempt.

Feature state machine on the board (A28, A34): feature-reopened (ready -> open), feature-branch-pushed and push-failed (push jobs), pull-request-closed, ideas-moved-to-new-feature, feature-abandoned. The policy pr-on-ready now pushes before it opens the pull request, and the push and fetch are effect jobs.

The policy start-process-on-launch now issues assign-task (task.yaml) and start-work (START.md) before start-agent-process: fleetd writes both files after the commit of the attempt in launching and before the launch (design, Supervision, dispatch order). The policy triage-on-gate-failed keeps its id and now starts a fix attempt of the task (A27); open-triage-task stays for a failure of the full gate.

worker-profiles marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again (adapter-conformance-passed, profile-marked-healthy), and a conformance drift becomes an idea (idea-on-adapter-drift). Profile validation refuses a profile on an OS where its sandbox is not supported (A37); it is a rule of plan validation, not an event.

plain_words.what: This step lists, in time order, everything that happens to 1 idea in fleetd: from 'horch idea add' to the feature merged in the primary branch, with the people and programs that cause each step.
plain_words.decided: The idea flow has 5 phases cut at 4 moments: the operator approves the assumptions, the plan commits, the verifier marks a task done, and the task branch of every task of the idea lands on its feature branch. Daemon supervision and adapter checks are a 6th phase outside the idea flow.
plain_words.assumed: An idea with no --to gets its feature row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions. A worker question waits 15 min for its sub-orchestrator before it goes to the operator.
plain_words.riskiest: The words 'ready' and 'landed' each name 2 or 3 states. The design now makes each message name the entity with the state. If a later step drops the entity, a status can say work is safe when it has not reached the primary branch.

deprecated.reason: Answered (orchestrator, D15): an idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions. Recorded in A8, H7, idea-captured and feature-opened.

Answered (orchestrator, D15): a worker question escalates to the operator after 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator. This is a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit. Recorded in H10 and escalate-question.
Answered (orchestrator, D15): decision D2, option B. Supervision and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outside the idea flow. Recorded in D2 and A3.
Answered (orchestrator, D15): decision D1, option A. 5 phases and 4 pivotal events. Recorded in D1 and A2.
